## Figure 1.8: Long-Term Net Transfers on Public and Publicly Guaranteed External Debt in Low- and Middle-Income Countries (Excluding China), by Creditor Type, 2015–25
Line chart

- **Units:** US$ (billion)
- **X-axis:** 2015 to 2025
- **Y-axis:** US$ (billion), from **−80** to **100**
- **Geographic/group coverage:** Low- and middle-income countries, **excluding China**
- **Series / legend:**
  - **PPG, multilateral + IMF**
  - **PPG, bonds**
  - **PPG, bilateral**
  - **PPG, commercial banks + other private creditors**
- **Reference line:** dashed horizontal line at **0**
- **Time span:** **2015–25**

### Series values
Values read from line positions are approximate and prefixed with **≈**. Values stated in the page text are copied exactly.

| Year | PPG, multilateral + IMF | PPG, bonds | PPG, bilateral | PPG, commercial banks + other private creditors |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2015 | ≈34 | ≈17 | ≈10 | ≈10 |
| 2016 | ≈31 | ≈49 | ≈12 | ≈−5 |
| 2017 | ≈24 | ≈96 | ≈21 | ≈−11 |
| 2018 | ≈49 | ≈32 | ≈16 | ≈13 |
| 2019 | ≈39 | ≈24 | ≈−1 | ≈−20 |
| 2020 | ≈94 | ≈−7 | ≈7 | ≈6 |
| 2021 | ≈35 | ≈−19 | ≈4 | ≈0 |
| 2022 | ≈60 | ≈−69 | ≈7 | ≈−5 |
| 2023 | ≈30 | ≈−9 | ≈8 | ≈−16 |
| 2024 | ≈21 | ≈−10 | ≈−7 | ≈−8 |
| 2025 | ≈25 | **70.1** | ≈−3 | **24.1** |

### Visual rankings and comparisons
- **Largest positive value in the figure:** **PPG, bonds** in **2017**, at **≈96**.
- **Second-largest positive peak:** **PPG, multilateral + IMF** in **2020**, at **≈94**.
- **Largest negative value:** **PPG, bonds** in **2022**, at **≈−69**.
- In **2025**, the highest net transfer is from **PPG, bonds (70.1)**, followed by:
  - **PPG, multilateral + IMF (≈25)**
  - **PPG, commercial banks + other private creditors (24.1)**
  - **PPG, bilateral (≈−3)**, the only negative series that year.
- **Bonds** are the most volatile series: strongly positive in **2015–19**, negative in **2020–24**, then sharply positive again in **2025**.
- **Multilateral + IMF** remains positive throughout the period, rising to a peak around **2020**, then easing but staying above zero in all years.
- **Bilateral** net transfers are modest throughout, mostly slightly positive until **2023**, then slightly negative in **2024** and **2025**.
- **Commercial banks + other private creditors** alternate between positive and negative values, with notable negatives in **2019** and **2023**, and a return to clearly positive territory in **2025**.

### Trends
- **PPG, bonds:** rises from **≈17** in 2015 to **≈96** in 2017, falls to **≈24** in 2019, turns negative in **2020**, reaches a trough around **2022**, stays slightly negative in **2023–24**, then rebounds sharply to **70.1** in **2025**.
- **PPG, multilateral + IMF:** positive every year; declines from **≈34** in 2015 to **≈24** in 2017, rises to **≈49** in 2018 and **≈94** in 2020, then moderates to **≈25** by 2025.
- **PPG, bilateral:** near **10–21** in **2015–18**, near zero in **2019**, small positives in **2020–23**, then slight negatives in **2024–25**.
- **PPG, commercial banks + other private creditors:** starts positive in **2015**, is negative in **2016–17**, positive in **2018**, sharply negative in **2019**, around zero to slightly negative in **2020–24**, then positive at **24.1** in **2025**.

**Source:** World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.  
**Note:** IMF = International Monetary Fund; PPG = public and publicly guaranteed.
